clue.text: Russian sailor, one of interest to entomologists?

parts.note: Red was the common label for a Soviet Russian
an admiral is a senior naval officer, a sailor of the highest rank

explanation.surface: A Soviet naval officer turns out to be someone who fascinates insect specialists.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is an example: a butterfly is one creature that entomologists study.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known European butterfly, and butterflies are insects studied by entomologists, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Dread being put up in list to produce perfumery

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the list word

parts.note: a roster is a list of names on duty

indicators.note: in a down clue, being put up means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: dread and awe both mean fearful reverence

explanation.surface: Fear is somehow listed in the process of making scent.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'put up' means written upwards. The definition is a perfumery product, not a perfume shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfumery here means a scented product, and this fragrant water distilled from petals is a classic toiletry scent.

clue.text: Commissionaire's seen fellow embracing nameless girl

definitions.note: read as commissionaire is, so the definition is commissionaire

indicators.note: embracing means one word wraps round another

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

indicators.note: nameless asks for N, the abbreviation for name, to be dropped

parts.note: Norma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A uniformed attendant has been spotted hugging a girl whose name has been forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commissionaire's seen' reads as 'the commissionaire is seen as': the 's is part of the link. 'nameless' takes N (name) out of NORMA, giving ORMA, which DON embraces.
explanation.definitionFit: A commissionaire is a uniformed attendant at the entrance of a hotel or theatre, the same job as a hotel's door attendant.

clue.text: Cars go for service

parts.note: Minis are small British cars
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: Vehicles are taken in for a routine check at the garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like the garage sense, but it means a branch of government.
explanation.definitionFit: A government department is a ministry, and such a department is a public service or branch of the civil service.

clue.text: This club has a famous name, and it can rely on a lunatic

definitions.text: This club has a famous name

indicators.note: lunatic means crazy, so the preceding letters are scrambled

parts.words: and it can rely on a

explanation.surface: A famous club is said to be able to rely on a madman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal and Ancient at St Andrews in Scotland is the famous golf club that long governed the rules of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews is one of the most famous golf clubs in the world.

clue.text: Extra pound for admitting, for instance, the old

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight
ye is an archaic form of the

explanation.surface: Someone pays an additional pound to let in examples of the ancient.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat; a leg bye is a run taken after the ball hits the batsman's body.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, extras are runs credited without the batsman hitting the ball, and this off-the-body run is one kind.

clue.text: Put name on house

definitions.meaning: to write your name on a document
in astrology, the twelve divisions of the zodiac, each with its symbol

explanation.definitionFit: To autograph something is to write your name on it; a zodiac division is called a house in astrology, its emblem a zodiacal symbol.

clue.text: Review 'orrible-smelling ingredient of drink

indicators.note: an ingredient is something contained in a mix, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to sup is to drink
humming means smelling bad; with the H dropped, cockney style, as the apostrophe in 'orrible shows

explanation.surface: A cockney complains of a foul-smelling component in a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'orrible tells you to drop the H of HUMMING too: humming is British slang for smelly.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's summary of the evidence at the end of a trial is a review of the case.

clue.text: Girl and I take shelter in church porch

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
taken as written
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A young woman and the speaker take cover in a church entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is a link word here, not a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name for a porch or chapel at the west end of some churches, an architectural term less familiar than the biblical region.

clue.text: Careless playing partners, one of them entrapped by attractive woman

parts.note: in bridge, North and South play as partners; here South is used

indicators.note: entrapped by means one piece is caught inside another

parts.note: a lovely is an attractive woman
the other of the bridge partners, North

explanation.surface: Two people at a game are careless, one of them having been seduced by a beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge partnerships are North-South and East-West; here S starts the answer and N goes inside LOVELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless about appearance or work means untidy and sloppy, which is the meaning of the answer.

clue.text: In a manner of speaking, bound to take a chance

indicators.note: the next word is to be heard as spoken, not as written

parts.note: to gambol is to leap or bound playfully

explanation.surface: Someone, figuratively, is certain to risk it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'certain', but it means leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To bet or risk something on an uncertain outcome is to take a chance.

clue.text: Someone ineffectual with naughty child

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A feeble person has a badly behaved child in tow.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeble, timid, ineffectual person is called a weakling, which is the informal meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Close to batsman, can twit

parts.note: silly describes cricket fielding positions very close to the batsman, such as silly point
a billy or billycan is a metal cooking can

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder stands near the batsman who is able to mock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' and 'twit' look like verbs; can is a billycan, a camping pot, and twit is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Twit and the answer are both affectionate British words for a foolish person.

clue.text: What's the point about passion fruit?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a tine is a point or prong of a fork or antler
anger is a passion, a strong emotion

explanation.surface: Someone asks what use passion fruit has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passion fruit' reads as one item; split it, with 'passion' in the wordplay and 'fruit' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small citrus fruit, a kind of mandarin orange, so a specific example of fruit.

clue.text: Tactless behaviour of lovelorn cowboy by lake

indicators.note: lorn means bereft; love is O, the zero score in tennis, so this takes O away

parts.note: a gaucho is a South American cowboy
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A heartbroken cowboy behaves clumsily beside the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lovelorn' looks like the cowboy's mood, but it tells you to remove O (love) from GAUCHO, leaving GAUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: This French-derived word means social awkwardness, a lack of tact or grace in behaviour.

clue.text: Stared at ruined lodge

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone gazed at a derelict lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To look at someone with obvious desire or intent is to stare at them in a leering way.

clue.text: Warship given orders, yet deviating

indicators.note: deviating means straying from course, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A naval vessel receives instructions but strays off course anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fast, manoeuvrable naval warship designed to escort fleets.

clue.text: Something really outstanding — cayenne, perhaps

definitions.meaning: an informal phrase for someone or something excellent or exciting
cayenne pepper is a fiery spice, an example of something spicy

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for something impressive or sexy, and taken literally means fiery food such as a spicy pepper.

clue.text: Rascal has an accent that's not British

indicators.note: not British means B, the abbreviation for British, is taken away

parts.note: a brogue is a regional accent, especially Irish

explanation.surface: A scoundrel speaks with a foreign accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing B from BROGUE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a dishonest or mischievous person, the same meaning as a scoundrel.

clue.text: I'm on sub — surprising form of transport

indicators.note: surprising suggests the words are unexpectedly jumbled

explanation.surface: A traveller is surprised to find themself on a submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the old full name for a bus, a public road vehicle carrying passengers.

clue.text: Disturbing gap if boys' attack launched here

indicators.note: disturbing means upsetting the order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unsettling gap appears where boys launched an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1961 invasion of Cuba by US-backed exiles was launched at this bay.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cuban bay was where the failed US-backed invasion of 1961 landed.

clue.text: Suggested, one member was guilty of terminological inexactitude

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
MP is a Member of Parliament
Churchill's famous euphemism for telling a lie in Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone hinted that a politician had been economical with the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminological inexactitude' was Winston Churchill's 1906 phrase avoiding the unparliamentary word 'lie'.
explanation.definitionFit: To suggest something without saying it outright is to hint at it, which is what the answer means.

clue.text: Tout de suite, as other Europeans put it

definitions.text: Tout de suite, as other Europeans put it

parts.words: Tout de suite, as other Europeans put it
parts.note: the French for at once, rendered as Spanish or Italian speakers would say it

explanation.definitionFit: This word, Spanish and Italian for ready or quick, is informal English for immediately, matching the French phrase.

clue.text: Having problems with ice

definitions.meaning: of a relationship or business, in serious trouble
of a drink, served over ice cubes

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a failing marriage or firm, and also a drink poured over ice cubes.

clue.text: Sticks back in box

indicators.note: back tells you to read the word from the end

parts.note: stick and rap both mean criticism or blame, as in taking stick or the rap

explanation.surface: Some sticks are put back into a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RAPS around; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To box lightly in practice, without full force, is to spar.

clue.text: King's given honour to man

definitions.note: read as king is, so the definition is king

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A monarch awards a decoration to a male subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King's given' reads as 'the king is given by'. He is the king of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream he is king of the fairies, husband of Titania.

clue.text: English character revealed in correspondence

parts.note: a quality is a trait or characteristic

explanation.surface: English personality shows through in letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondence' suggests letters, but it means matching or parity.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence in the sense of exact match or parity between things means sameness of value or standing.

clue.text: Man perhaps, with German name, leaving Northern city

indicators.note: leaving means the name goes out of the city's word

parts.note: Carlisle is a city in the far north of England
Carl is a German form of Charles

explanation.surface: A man with a German name leaves a city in the North.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, the island in the Irish Sea; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is one example of an island, so the definition gives an instance of the answer.

clue.text: Unfrocked monk is not working

definitions.meaning: a monk expelled from his religious order

explanation.definitionFit: A defrocked monk has been put out of his religious order, and a broken machine carries a sign saying it is broken.
